brief.headline: Push PIK PLASTICS to match the ₹7.62/NOS price TPAC already gives us on the same amber bottle — that saves ₹8.48 L a year.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match the ₹7.62/NOS price TPAC Packaging India Pvt Ltd. gives us for the PET BOT AMBER 250ML/28MM WITH SHR SL 01 — our top SKU with them.
priceAsk.target: ₹7.62/NOS (down from their ₹8.49/NOS) — closes an 11.5% gap and saves ₹8.48 L a year across all items.
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹7.62/NOS to TPAC for the identical bottle. PIK's ₹8.49/NOS is 11.5% higher for the same thing. Market research shows similar PP caps trade at ₹0.85–0.95/pc (typical band), with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — so our ask is in line with what the market will bear.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep the current 30 Days After Receipt — no reason to ease terms when we're asking them to cut price.

brief.financialLeverage: PIK PLASTICS publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. That means we build our case purely on the prices in front of us: they charge ₹8.49/NOS while TPAC charges ₹7.62/NOS for the same bottle. Our ₹1.92 Cr annual spend with them is real money, but without knowing their size we can't say how big a customer we are. The good news: we have four strong alternates already qualified (Manjushree, Mold-Tek, Hitech, Pearl) and six more leads to check out — so we're not stuck if they won't move. Push firmly on price, and make it clear we're lining up a second source because we don't know enough about their business to rely on them alone.

evidence.point: We pay PIK ₹8.49/NOS for PET BOT AMBER 250ML/28MM WITH SHR SL 01, but TPAC gives us ₹7.62/NOS for the identical bottle — an 11.5% gap.
Closing that gap across all items saves us ₹8.48 L a year.
Our total annual spend with PIK is ₹1.92 Cr — enough to demand the best price we already pay elsewhere.
Market research shows 28 mm PP caps typically ask ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume — our target is within that range.
PIK publishes no financials, so we can't gauge their health or how much they need our business.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue) — makes pharma bottles, caps and preforms; health score B (65/100); already a second source for packaging and the top candidate to split this business.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue) making pails, containers and pharma packaging; health score B (73/100) — strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: IVL Dhunseri Petrochem Industries Private Limited (market lead)
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — manufacturer in India-East; medium confidence. Could be a direct PET source if PIK won't budge.

risks: PIK publishes no financials — we don't know if they're healthy or fragile. Push hard on price, but watch for signs they can't sustain the business; have Manjushree ready to step in.

We spend ₹1.92 Cr with them but don't know their total revenue — if we're a tiny customer, our leverage is limited. Lead with the TPAC benchmark (a fact they can't argue) rather than threatening to walk.
The ₹8.48 L saving assumes they match TPAC across all SKUs. If they only move on the big bottle (₹7.19 L of the ₹8.48 L), we still win most of it — but get a commitment on the rest too.

Six market-backup leads (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are unqualified — don't mention them in the room until we've checked them out; use the four qualified alternates instead.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're here because you're charging us ₹8.49 a bottle for an item TPAC supplies at ₹7.62 — we'd like to understand that gap and get you to the same price.
